scope: Sanitized snapshot of the original development workspace. A fresh installation starts with its own empty job history; the historical jobs and checkpoints are not bundled.

latest_experiment.name: SELF-PPO
latest_experiment.note: Latest saved training experiment in the audited main workspace. Historical paused state, not a running job in this installation. No final held-out test is claimed for this unfinished job.

methods.title: Collect existing models and demonstrations
methods.summary: Register versioned bots, select teachers, and record their legal observations and executed actions in mixed table configurations.
methods.evidence: FirstDatasetV2 completed with 310,500 table-hand episodes and 2,952,868 decision records across 4-, 5-, and 6-player tables.
methods.limitations: Teachers are sources of behavior, not guaranteed optimal play. Upstream attribution and redistribution rights belong in the source registry.

methods.title: Behaviour cloning (BC)
methods.summary: Train one neural policy to imitate the selected teachers' actions, using a grouped train/validation/test split.
methods.evidence: BC_1 completed 10 epochs. BC_2 finished early after 76 of 100 requested epochs and selected epoch 75. Both used FirstDatasetV2.
methods.limitations: Action agreement measures imitation, not winnings. The same decision data contains correlated decisions and duplicate-deal groups.

methods.title: PPO against existing bots
methods.summary: Warm-start the actor from BC, collect new poker hands against frozen registered opponents, and update the actor with a learned critic.
methods.evidence: Completed 10k, 100k and 600k hand budgets; both five-player and mixed 4/5/6-player training configurations were tried. Later runs also used game-placement rewards.
methods.limitations: Training budget does not identify the selected checkpoint. Chip-reward scores and placement-reward scores use different units and must not share a leaderboard.

methods.title: Self-play PPO
methods.summary: Train one learner against frozen copies of its policy; refresh the copies after each update. Mixed mode can add historical policies and registered bots.
methods.evidence: SELF-PPO is paused at 479,000 of 600,000 hand episodes across 4/5/6 players. Pure self-play was used; mixed self-play is implemented but has no main training job in this snapshot.
methods.limitations: Self-play reward alone is not a strength ranking. Validation uses fixed external opponents. The latest saved model and validation-selected best model can differ.

methods.title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)
methods.summary: Repeat matched 100-hand games with different learner action samples, compare rewards within each group, and update the policy without a value critic.
methods.evidence: Dashboard, training worker, resume/export support and focused tests are present. The audited main database contains zero GRPO jobs.
methods.limitations: This is an experimental poker adaptation. A completed training loop or a reward difference within one group would not establish better play.

methods.title: PHH data and offline lookup
methods.summary: Convert compatible public hand histories into observations; imitate them with BC or build action-frequency tables offline for fast lookup during play.
methods.evidence: PHH import is implemented in the dashboard. Separate PHH_Lookup_v1 and six stricter lookup agents were built and compatibility-tested during development.
methods.limitations: Standalone tables and data are not bundled. The strict all-source scan retained only six-player Pluribus hands; v1 has direct 4/5/6-player examples. Frequencies are not solved action values.

methods.title: Search: rollouts, ISMCTS and OOS
methods.summary: Use sampled hidden-card worlds to compare simulated continuations, build an information-set tree, or update an online outcome-sampling strategy.
methods.evidence: Search_Rollouts, Search_ISMCTS and Search_OOS were packaged as standalone bots. Each has a saved 180-hand SDK compatibility check across 4/5/6 players.
methods.limitations: These are small approximate implementations with limited computation. Compatibility checks do not demonstrate equilibrium play or tournament strength.

methods.title: Frozen PPO + lookup + rollouts
methods.summary: Compare PPO alone, PPO + lookup, PPO + rollouts and PPO + both, keeping PPO weights frozen in every variant.
methods.evidence: All four use PPO_5p_600_000_v3. Saved checks report 33 focused tests and 720 SDK hands with legal actions and no bot failures.
methods.limitations: No retraining was done. Lookup coverage is sparse and rollout opponents are approximate. These checks do not identify a strongest variant.
